commands.review_summary:
This PR wraps the `secrets apply` plan-file parse and `capability model auth status` captured-output parse in try/catch blocks, and adds two CLI regression tests.

PR surface: Source +14, Tests +35. Total +49 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: current main directly parses the secrets plan file and the captured model-auth JSON-looking output, so malformed inputs can throw before friendly handling. I did not run the CLI because this review is read-only.

target.title: fix(cli): harden JSON.parse in secrets apply and model-auth status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two unguarded `JSON.parse()` calls in the CLI can crash with raw `SyntaxError` exceptions instead of producing user-friendly errors or graceful fallbacks:

1. **`src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:56`** — `readPlanFile()` calls `JSON.parse(raw)` on a plan file read from disk. A corrupt/malformed plan file throws a raw `SyntaxError` with stack trace instead of a friendly error message telling the user how to regenerate the plan.

2. **`src/cli/capability-cli.ts:938`** — `runModelAuthStatus()` captures stdout from `modelsStatusCommand`, finds a line starting with `{`, and parses it. If the captured output contains a malformed JSON fragment, the `model-auth status` command crashes instead of gracefully returning `{}`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both are minimal defensive wrappings:
- `readPlanFile`: wrap in try/catch, throw a friendly `Error` with the file path and the regenerate command
- `runModelAuthStatus`: wrap in try/catch, return `{}` as graceful degradation (caller already handles empty results)

## Evidence

### Real terminal output (7 assertions, real file I/O):
```
$ npx tsx _proof-harden-jsonparse.ts
=== Proof: Hardened JSON.parse in CLI ===

secrets-cli readPlanFile (real file round-trip):
PASS   Before fix: raw SyntaxError on corrupt file
PASS   After fix: friendly Error with file path and malformed JSON guidance
PASS   Valid plan file parses correctly (no regression)

capability-cli runModelAuthStatus (unparseable CLI output):
PASS   Before fix: SyntaxError on unparseable output
PASS   After fix: graceful {} when captured line is not valid JSON
PASS   After fix: valid JSON still parses correctly (no regression)
PASS   After fix: no JSON-like lines returns empty object

=== Results: 7 passed, 0 failed ===
```

### Regression tests (in existing CLI test files):
- `src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts`: corrupt plan file → friendly error with "malformed JSON" and file path (no SyntaxError)
- `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`: unparseable model auth status output → `{}` (no crash)

## Merge Risk

Low — defensive try/catch wrappers. Valid JSON paths are unchanged. No new dependencies, no logic changes.
